name: Shelf Chairlift
description: A repurposed industrial chairlift running along the exterior of Shelf tower blocks, carrying residents up and down the building faces on open-air seats suspended from a continuous cable. Originally installed by a resident who worked in ski resort maintenance, the chairlift system has expanded to cover three buildings. It's terrifying, wind-exposed, and saves elderly residents a forty-story stairclimb when the elevators break down — which is always. Riders sit in the open air, feet dangling, watching the city spread out below them. Some find it peaceful. Others never open their eyes.
capacity: 2 passengers per chair, chairs every 15 meters
common_usage: Vertical transit for elderly and disabled residents, cargo hauling, building access when elevators fail.
story_hooks: The chairlift operator is the most connected person in The Shelf — they see everyone coming and going and have been keeping a log for ten years
Someone sabotages the chairlift cable and the investigation reveals the target wasn't a person — it was something being carried in a cargo chair at 3 AM
